title: ERC-8309 vantage-authority companion -- resolution envelope (§5 E1-E6)
description: Derived from the bytes the reference implementation actually emits (services/vantage_resolution.py, ResolutionEnvelope.to_obj), then verified against it -- not written from the prose and assumed to match. Any disagreement between this schema and the emitter is a finding, and the check script treats it as one.

x-canonical-serializer.note: §5 binds the serializer EXPLICITLY PER SCHEMA and never infers it. Recorded inside the schema on purpose: a schema that does not name its own serializer forces every consumer to infer one, which is the exact defect the per-schema rule was ratified to remove. RFC 8785 emits no trailing byte; encodeJsonUtf8Lf emits exactly one 0x0a and is a DIFFERENT, separately-bound serializer -- the same object digests to unrelated hashes under the two.

schema.description: MUST be the schema binding, never the document identifier. `erc-8309-vantage-authority-companion` names the DOCUMENT and does not resolve as a schema -- the six-binding collapse this const exists to make unrepresentable.

version.description: Self-identifying so an envelope can be pinned. §5.

e1_agreement_object.description: E1: WHAT is being agreed about. A resolution over an unnamed object is not checkable.

e2_membership.description: E2: who counts. null is a legitimate value -- Profile A makes no membership judgment -- and is distinct from the key being absent, which would leave it inferable.

global.description: E3: independence is declared PER VANTAGE CLASS (§8), never globally. A global claim is nonconformant, so `true` is unrepresentable here rather than merely discouraged.

finality_rule.description: E4/§6a: null means NO finality is claimed. Absence of a finality rule must never be read as finality -- §6a evaluations are immutable but supersedable, with no implied finality.

window_basis.description: E5: a window measured over SIGNED TIMESTAMPS is nonconformant, because backdating and late arrival are indistinguishable under one. Enforced here as an exclusion rather than left to the consumer.

e6_evidence_requirements.description: E6: what evidence a conformant reading requires. An empty list would mean 'no evidence required', which is not a resolution.
